title: Derived Hom for a Koszul-regular closed immersion
statement: Let i:Z\to Y be a Koszul-regular closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. Let \mathcal I be its ideal sheaf [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], let C_i=i^*(\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2) be the conormal sheaf [def-pc-module-pullback], and let N_i=\operatorname{SheafHom}_{\mathcal O_Z}(C_i,\mathcal O_Z) be its dual [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. If the rank of C_i is the locally constant function r, then there is a canonical isomorphism in the derived category of quasi-coherent complexes on Y [def-pc-derived-category, def-pur-derived-internal-hom], compatible with the i_*\mathcal O_Z-module structures, $$R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_Y}(i_*\mathcal O_Z,\mathcal O_Y)\cong i_*\bigl(\bigwedge^r N_i[-r]\bigr).$$

source.place: Tag 0BQZ, lemma-regular-immersion-ext (Koszul-complex computation of the derived sheaf Hom)

proof.text: By Koszul-regularity, every point of Y has an affine open neighbourhood U=\operatorname{Spec}(A) on which the ideal of Z\cap U is generated by a finite Koszul-regular sequence f_1,\ldots,f_r. The perfectness statement [lem-sc-koszul-regular-closed-immersion-perfect] identifies i_*\mathcal O_Z|_U with the bounded Koszul complex K_A(f_\bullet), whose terms are finite free A-modules.

source.place: Tag 068C, together with Tag 0BQZ local Koszul model

proof.text: Apply the affine dual-Koszul calculation [lem-sc-koszul-regular-sequence-dual-complex] on U. Since i_*\mathcal O_Z|_U is quasi-isomorphic to the bounded complex of finite free modules \widetilde{K_A(f_\bullet)} (Step 1), the total sheaf Hom complex \mathcal Hom^\bullet(\widetilde{K_A(f_\bullet)},\mathcal O_U) represents R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(i_*\mathcal O_Z|_U,\mathcal O_U) by [lem-sc-derived-hom-finite-free-model], and for finite free terms this sheaf Hom complex is the sheaf associated to \operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(K_A(f_\bullet),A). The child computes the latter in D(A) as the shifted top exterior power of the B-dual of I/I^2, viewed by restriction of scalars from B=A/I. Under the affine identifications, I/I^2 is the restriction of the conormal sheaf C_i and its B-dual is the restriction of N_i, so the local result is R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(i_*\mathcal O_Z|_U,\mathcal O_U)\simeq i_*(\bigwedge^rN_i[-r])|_U, compatibly with the i_*\mathcal O_Z-module structures; in particular \mathcal H^q(R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_Y}(i_*\mathcal O_Z,\mathcal O_Y))|_U=0 for q\neq r, using [lem-sc-derived-internal-hom-restrict-open].

Isomorphisms in the derived category do not glue directly, so glue on cohomology sheaves. Put R=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_Y}(i_*\mathcal O_Z,\mathcal O_Y). By Step 2, on each U of the cover \mathcal H^q(R)|_U=0 for q\neq r, where r is the locally constant rank (the length of the local regular sequence); hence R has cohomology sheaves concentrated in degree r on each connected-rank piece, and the canonical truncation maps give R\cong\mathcal H^r(R)[-r] in the derived category (elementary). Step 2 also gives sheaf isomorphisms \mathcal H^r(R)|_U\cong i_*\bigwedge^rN_i|_U of i_*\mathcal O_Z-modules. On an overlap, compare them on affine opens W=\operatorname{Spec}A' that are standard opens in both charts: by the localization functoriality of [lem-sc-koszul-regular-sequence-dual-complex] both restrict to the isomorphism \operatorname{Ext}^r_{A'}(A'/I',A')\cong\bigwedge^r N attached to the two restricted generating sequences, and by the child's independence of the chosen generating sequence these coincide; restriction of R to opens is compatible by [lem-sc-derived-internal-hom-restrict-open]. Morphisms of sheaves glue, so the local isomorphisms glue to a canonical isomorphism \mathcal H^r(R)\cong i_*\bigwedge^rN_i of i_*\mathcal O_Z-modules, whence R\cong i_*(\bigwedge^rN_i[-r]).
